defects.detail: note on 'pasek z ogórkami' calls it 'the friar's humble, food-laden belt'; the 'ogórki' are the cucumber-shaped knots of the cord, and the source says nothing about food
'Grają chartów wypadłszy wesoło skowycze' (the greyhounds' yelps ring out merrily as they rush out) -> 'The greyhounds play, having rushed out happily whimpering'
'dojeżdżaczów smycze' (the whippers-in's leashes) -> 'the leash-holders'

reason: Faithful verse rendering. The added note misreads the knotted cord as a food-laden belt, and two hunting lines are slightly misparsed.

defects.detail: citations 'l. si cui 92. ff. de condit. et demonstr. l. nec avus 4. C. de Emancip. liber.' replaced by 'and other citations'

reason: The legal argument about consent, compulsion of the father and emancipation is rendered accurately. One run of citations is collapsed into 'and other citations'.
Weber's argument on the family entail, Wakuf, Becker, monopolies and Frankfurt is rendered in full and accurately. No errors found.

defects.detail: the Col. V translation opening ''To Eusebius, adjutant ... 4,440 lbs. Copy of the receipt: Aurelius Eusebius ... I have received from you 120 baskets. Mecheir 20.' is missing; the note jumps from apparatus '29. ῦπο Pap.' straight to 'Given under my hand. To Pyrus'
the apparatus from '34. ἴδοτος Pap.' through 'IV.' and 'V.' to 'VI. 25. l. Νομίου Τού[σκου' is dropped
apparatus 'l.' (read) is rendered as the numeral '1.', and Greek lemmata are glossed as words ('κυριῶ Pap.' -> 'lords, Pap.')

reason: The apparatus is cut off mid-list and merged into the receipts, so the Eusebius receipt (4,440 lbs, 120 baskets) is lost. The commentary notes are fine.
Hippocrates on Asian laws and courage and the Sauromatae women is rendered faithfully through the final 'stops'. No errors found.

defects.detail: 'un gruzzolo di scudi' (a purse of crowns/coins) -> 'a stash of shields'
'scala franca della paura' (free port of fear) -> 'a frank staircase of fear'

reason: The narrative is accurate throughout. Two literalisms are wrong: 'scudi' (coins) rendered as 'shields', and 'scala franca' (free port) as 'frank staircase'.
The tract on hat-honour, Jacob and Esau, the two Adams and the original languages is rendered faithfully. The notes and glosses are interpretive only.
The source is English with Greek fragments. It is reproduced intact (Σμ. given as Sm.), which is correct.

defects.detail: 'Αὐρηλίῳ Σαραπάμμωνι μητρὸς Ταπαμῶνος καὶ Τκαλῆτι ἐκ μητρὸς Θαήσιος' (to Sarapammon, mother Tapamon, and to Tkales, mother Thaesis) -> 'Sarapammon son of Tapamon and Tkaletis, whose mother is Thaesis', which merges the second freed slave into a parent
'ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ (sc. the slave)' -> 'for her...', which drops the editor's '(sc. the slave)'

reason: The commentary is faithful. In the Edmondstone deed the addressee list is misparsed, turning Tkales from a manumitted slave into a parent.

defects.detail: Column 3 (the Ottoman Turkish verse rendering, e.g. 'پس پور مشهد را چون اول رسول', 'حرص چاک ایلیر قناعت روی') is not translated at all
'لیک اول پند بدهندش که بین سحر را زما میاموز' (but first they warn: beware, do not learn magic from us) -> 'But take that bad advice as a guide, Do not learn magic'
garbled 'وز بلیسی چهره خوب سجود' / 'همچو سیم نام پا و تن زده' -> 'from Iblis, there is good prostration in the face' / 'Like a name on a foot or a body', given as confident verse

reason: Only the two Persian columns are translated; the Turkish column is dropped. Several garbled hemistichs are passed off as verse. My reading of Persian and Ottoman manuscript text is moderate.

defects.detail: idiom 'Damals konntest du mir noch gestohlen werden' (back then I couldn't have cared less about you) -> 'Back then you could still be stolen from me'
'an den Hals geworfen' (threw her at me) is rendered literally as 'throw her onto my neck'

reason: The dialogue is accurate except for two German idioms rendered literally, one of which changes the sense.

defects.detail: 'οὐδ' ἐπεχείρησεν ἔτι τοῦ ἀντιδιῃρημένου τῇ ἰσχύϊ ... προσηγορίας δηλῶσαι' (nor did he attempt to state the names of the species opposed to strength) -> '[He] attempted to declare further the soothing that remains', which drops the negation and misreads the noun
Latin 'e regione paucitati opposita' (directly opposed to fewness) -> 'opposed to fewness in that region'
'Commoderatio namque deligationem' (page ends) -> 'For the symmetry [provides] the goodness of the binding', which supplies a completion

reason: The Greek opening clause is inverted and garbled ('attempted ... the soothing'). The rest of the Greek and the parallel Latin are rendered correctly.

defects.detail: '天下多得一察焉以自好' (many in the world seize on one aspect and examine it to please themselves) -> 'the world obtains much, yet examines it [only] to satisfy one's own desires'
'其數散於天下而設於中國者' (those of its measures scattered in the world and set up in the Middle Kingdom) -> 'Those who establish themselves in the Central Kingdom are the hundred schools'

reason: This Zhuangzi 'Tianxia' passage is mostly correct. '多得一察' and the opening clause are misparsed.

defects.detail: Row 45's answers 'De Oorsake/Causa, de Kracht/Vis, het Wercktuygh/Instrumentum' and all of rows 46-48 plus most of 49 (Helft, Stuck, Bijteiken; Beginsel, Midden, Eynde; Ordening, Tijdt, Plaetse; Getal, Mate, Gewicht; Oogenblik, Wijl-tijdt, Uur, Dagh) are missing
'What is in motion?' is answered 'The Week / Septimana, the Month' (spliced from row 49)

reason: About a third of the vocabulary table (rows 45-49) is dropped, and the remainder is spliced so that 'motion' gets 'Week, Month'. The rest of the table is correct.

defects.detail: 'lamellis ... albocarneis' (whitish flesh-coloured gills) -> 'white-fleshed lamellae'
'non sine verit. spec.' (not without likelihood, verisimilitude) -> 'not without veracity of the species'

'Odor mihi, pulvere sternut. scatenti, obsoletus' (odour faint to me, having a cold from sneezing powder) -> 'Odor, to me, abounding in sneezing powder, obsolete', which makes the smell full of powder

reason: The mycological descriptions are accurate overall. There are a few slips: 'albocarneis', 'verit. spec.', and the sneezing-powder aside.
